items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: Herman's, who was the baker shop across the street, we would go there and if we didn't have any money we could go there and say, 'I'll pay you at the end of the week, Mr. Herman.'

ctx.x: Yeah, you'd get a dollar and a quarter. It was a whole lot of money. With a dollar and a quarter, I'd be able to take my girl and buy her a dish of ice cream. Or if I got enough money, I could go and buy her oyster stew. There was a fellow on South Street that had a place they called Early's.

And we went there so often that we could have fun there. And we were big timers there. And Herman's, who was the baker shop across the street, we would go there and if we didn't have any money we could go there and say, "I'll pay you at the end of the week, Mr. Herman." Or, Mr. Early. And they'd let it go and the little girl would stretch her eyes, her eyes would pop open, and she'd say, "Oh, they're big timers." See?
